_note: Ready-made groups with published sources (government, MoSPI, ONS, and the PRICE ICE 360 survey via news reports). Shares are starting points: set your own for your customers. Checked 18 November 2026.

values.name: Tier 1 metro (Mumbai / Delhi / Bengaluru / Chennai / Hyderabad / Kolkata / Ahmedabad / Pune)

facts.text: The government classes 8 cities as X (Tier 1) for house rent allowance, the highest rate: Mumbai, Delhi, Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Ahmedabad and Pune.
Urban Indians spend on average ₹6,996 per person per month (2023-24), about 70% more than rural Indians (₹4,122).

values.name: Tier 2 city (e.g. Jaipur / Lucknow / Nagpur / Indore / Kochi)

facts.text: Cities classed Y (Tier 2) by the government get a lower house rent allowance rate than the 8 X-class metros.
Urban Indians spend on average ₹6,996 per person per month (2023-24), about 70% more than rural Indians (₹4,122).
All cities not classed X or Y are Z class (Tier 3), with the lowest house rent allowance.
Urban Indians spend on average ₹6,996 per person per month (2023-24), about 70% more than rural Indians (₹4,122).
Rural Indians spend on average ₹4,122 per person per month (2023-24); the rural-urban gap has narrowed from 84% in 2011-12 to about 70%.

india_income_tiers.title: India income tiers (household, Tier 1 to Tier 4)

segments.name: Tier 1: rich household (over ₹30 lakh a year)

facts.text: Rich households (over ₹30 lakh a year) spend about ₹20.5 lakh a year on average, almost 3 times a middle-class household (PRICE ICE 360 survey, 2020-21).

segments.name: Tier 2: middle-class household (₹5 to 30 lakh a year)

facts.text: Middle-class households earn ₹5 to 30 lakh a year; the middle class was about 31% of India's population in 2020-21 (PRICE ICE 360 survey).

segments.name: Tier 3: aspiring household (₹1.25 to 5 lakh a year)

facts.text: Aspirer households earn ₹1.25 to 5 lakh a year: above the lowest-income group but below the middle class (PRICE ICE 360 survey classes).

segments.name: Tier 4: low-income household (under ₹1.25 lakh a year)

facts.text: The lowest-income households (under ₹1.25 lakh a year) spend about ₹82,300 a year on average (PRICE ICE 360 survey, 2020-21).

uk_london.title: London vs rest of the UK

facts.text: London had the highest spending per person of the English regions in 2023 (£28,600) and the highest household saving ratio (23.9%).
In 2023, spending per person ranged from £19,842 (North East) to £28,600 (London) across English regions; Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland were about £22,700 to £23,500.
